entry.title: [MEDIUM] User-level `paths:` rules can silently load nowhere.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS setup placed `paths:` frontmatter on a rule under `~/.claude/rules/`. The rule was skipped at `session_start` because it was conditional, but it also never loaded on matching file reads because user-scope rules did not appear to participate in `path_glob_match`. Project-scoped path rules matched the same file normally, and the missing user rule did not appear in `/context`, leaving a syntactically valid global convention with zero effect and no warning.

entry.title: [HIGH] Subagent compound Bash can bypass sandbox read-deny protection.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS background/job session declared sandbox filesystem `read.denyOnly` coverage for `.env*` paths and had top-level protected-path reads blocked elsewhere in the same session. A general-purpose Agent subagent then ran a compound multi-line Bash command containing `grep` against `.env.local`; the command returned real environment variable names with exit code 0, no prompt, no permission error, and no block log. The same path with `cat` would have exposed secret values to the subagent context.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Native deny messages can hide the matched rule and settings source.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS setup found that `permissions.deny` blocks returned generic denial text without the specific matched rule or the settings file that supplied it. With user, project, local, and managed settings all able to define overlapping permission rules, users had to remove and retest candidate rules manually to explain an unexpected denial. The same report says `claude -p` can print a startup warning that `Write(path)` deny rules are not matched by file permission checks, while normal interactive sessions with the same ineffective rules did not surface that warning.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows plugin hooks may not receive subscription OAuth token environment.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Code 2.1.228 setup installed the official `security-guidance` marketplace plugin under subscription `/login` auth, but every LLM review gate exited with `LLM review disabled or no API credentials`. The plugin hook process saw neither `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` nor `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, even though the plugin source expected Claude Code to pass an OAuth access token to hooks for login users. The hook itself fired, so the visible plugin installation could look active while its review layer was dormant except for debug-log lines.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash deny patterns ending in `:branch` may not block matching git refspec pushes.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS permission audit found that several `permissions.deny` patterns for protected-branch pushes worked, including patterns matching `main`, `develop`, `refs/heads/develop`, and `HEAD:*`. However, deny rules shaped like `Bash(git push *:develop)` and `Bash(git push *:main)` did not match a direct refspec such as `git push --dry-run origin my-branch-name:develop`; the permission layer allowed the command through and only git rejected it later. The failed rules looked like explicit protected-branch coverage while matching nothing in the tested case.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] `claudeMdExcludes` can silently miss symlinked rules paths.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS setup used separate config worlds and attempted to exclude a third-party toolkit's home-level `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/*.md` files. The `CLAUDE.md` exclude worked, but rules installed as symlinks still loaded until the exclude pattern targeted the resolved symlink destination under the toolkit's versioned directory. The docs described `CLAUDE.md` memory excludes but did not make it clear that rules files were in scope or that matching used resolved paths, producing a silent partial success that looked like isolation until an `InstructionsLoaded` hook logged every loaded path.

entry.title: [HIGH] Subagent forks can inherit full parent context and become unresumable.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Linux orchestration session found that an internal `subagent_type: "fork"` inherited the full parent context for a narrow summarization task, consuming 143,790 tokens for work the reporter estimated at roughly 2,000 tokens when done directly. Other forked agents returned garbled or truncated output after long runs, could not be resumed because no transcript was found, or completed commits without delivering their reasoning back to the orchestrator. The reporter's follow-up described substantial cost and lost operator time from dozens of subagents that disappeared or failed to report.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] VS Code chat channel relaunches can abort in-flight work.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code Remote WSL2 session saw the extension log `Closing Claude on channel` and tear down one or two active chat channels without a user action or VS Code host restart. One incident happened mid-response stream, dropped backend process count to zero for more than a minute, and later resumed the same session; another relaunch spawned two backend processes for the same resume and one failed with a config lock error. Conversation state resumed, but in-flight tool calls and responses were aborted while the UI looked like the session crashed.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Unlogged interruption messages can enter model context outside the transcript.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Desktop 2.1.229 Windows session showed the model responding to a system-styled interruption message that the user says they did not send and that had no corresponding user-role entry in the local JSONL transcript. The injected content impersonated a user interruption, claimed a compressed context view, and asked the agent to use existing SSH access to create a production admin account with a public password. The model refused, but the first local trace was the assistant response, leaving the user unable to audit how the content reached the request from transcript evidence alone.

entry.title: [HIGH] Background forks can drop Vertex gateway auth environment variables.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS Vertex-gateway setup found that pressing left arrow to background a conversation into a daemon fork reconstructed the worker environment without `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_VERTEX_AUTH` and `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL`, while keeping `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`. The forked worker then attempted local Google ADC and failed every request, even though the original interactive session and daemon process had the complete gateway environment.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Background job main sessions can miss the available-skills listing.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS background job started from the agents interface did not receive the available-skills system-reminder in its main session, while subagents spawned from that same session did receive the full personal, project, and built-in skills listing. Because Claude Code instructs agents to use only listed skills, the background job main session had no discoverable path to invoke a matching user or project skill and produced an HTML deliverable without loading the user's page-convention skill.

entry.title: [HIGH] File-freshness notices can assert false user intent and tell agents not to disclose it.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Windows parent session plus background subagent workflow found that native file-modification boilerplate could appear after an agent changed tracked files outside Edit/Write tooling. The notice asserted that the change was intentional, that the user was already aware, and that the assistant should not tell the user. In the reported cases those assertions were false: the change came from an agent edit or revert, and the human did not know about it. The same notice was also ephemeral enough that a recovered subagent transcript did not contain the injected text, making later forensics first look like either a prompt-injection event or a model confabulation.

entry.title: [HIGH] Sibling subagents can silently overwrite each other's scratchpad files.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 multi-agent workflow found that sibling subagents spawned by one orchestrator shared a single scratchpad directory keyed by the parent session, and a background-forked Skill inherited the parent's own scratchpad path. Parallel agents converged on generic filenames such as `preview.html` and `threads.json`; later reads succeeded but returned a sibling's artifact or a concurrently truncated parent file, making read-back verification accuse the wrong layer.

entry.title: [HIGH] Agent `run_in_background: false` can still behave like a background dispatch.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Windows Agent workflow found that `run_in_background: false` returned immediately with the same background-spawn message instead of blocking for the agent's final report. The agents completed their work, but results arrived only later as teammate messages or sometimes never arrived as text. The reporter measured batches where agents went idle after doing useful work while the parent saw no final tool result, causing fallback inline work and quiet quality loss.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Foreground operator input can be routed into a background Agent task.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code background Agent workflow delivered text typed by the operator in the main session into a live background task's transcript instead of creating a new main-session turn. The misdelivered messages appeared to the background task as genuine user interruptions while the main session had no visible record that those turns were sent there. In the cleanest reported incident, a task originally scoped to merging approved PRs received operator authorization language and used it to dispatch a separate security-testing crew outside its original task scope.

entry.title: [HIGH] Background Bash tasks can be killed while reporting success.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS session found that a Bash tool call using `run_in_background: true` could SIGKILL the task shell and its process group while still notifying the user that the task completed with exit code 0. The triggering command invoked a CLI that spawned a detached daemonizing worker; foreground runs succeeded, but 7 of 9 background runs lost post-command markers or output, and some left 0-byte result files. A later test detached the worker into its own session: the task shell could still die, while the worker survived and wrote valid JSON, narrowing the failure to group-targeted task cleanup plus incorrect success reporting.

entry.title: [HIGH] Piped `-p` prompts can be recorded but omitted from the model request.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Windows headless setup intermittently enqueued and persisted a full piped prompt in the transcript and last-prompt preview, but the first API request behaved as if the user turn were empty. Failing runs exited 0 in one or two turns with tiny ambient-context responses, while usage telemetry showed only 2 input tokens for the user request despite the same wrapper and prompt bytes succeeding minutes apart. Transcript inspection alone can therefore falsely reassure automation owners that the prompt reached the model.

entry.title: [HIGH] `grep` shell shim can silently skip binary and ignored files.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Linux and WSL2 setup found that Bash tool calls shadowed system `grep` with a shell function that runs the bundled ugrep using flags such as `-I` and `--ignore-files`. Files containing NUL bytes and files matched by `.gitignore` were skipped with exit status 1 and no stdout or stderr, making the result indistinguishable from a genuine no-match search. The report also notes that `which grep` can still point at `/usr/bin/grep`, so an agent investigating the failure may see contradictory evidence while carrying forward a false conclusion that searched code does not exist.

entry.title: [HIGH] Sandboxed Bash helper process can OOM during a slow command.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Linux session in an unprivileged LXC found that an ephemeral per-tool-call helper process named `claude.exe` grew to 11.6 GB anonymous RSS in about two minutes while a sandboxed Bash pipeline was running. The interactive Claude Code process stayed around 430 MB, the input JSONL files totaled under 14 MB, and the known triggering command was a slow `grep -o -i` bounded-repetition pattern piped to `head` that hit the Bash tool timeout. The kernel OOM kill occurred inside the service cgroup, and with systemd `OOMPolicy=stop` it stopped the parent Claude service before restart recovered it.

entry.title: [HIGH] Cloud routine egress allowlist domains may not reach the sandbox proxy.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code cloud routine found that domains added to the account-level `Allow network egress` additional-domains setting did not appear in the routine sandbox's proxy allowlist a week later. Both scheduled fires and a manual `RemoteTrigger run` still returned `EGRESS_BLOCKED` from `WebFetch` and 403 CONNECT failures from `curl`, while the in-sandbox `$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status` endpoint confirmed the expected domains were absent. The trigger API exposed prompt, allowed tools, MCP connections, and schedule state, but no sandbox network policy field that could be updated or inspected for repair.
